h: Making the most of Southend's seafront
p: Southend became a city in 2022, but it hasn't lost its cheerful seaside spirit. Getting here is easy from London, with trains running into Southend Central and Southend Victoria, both handy for the High Street and The Royals. It makes a cracking day trip without a car.

Once you're down at the front, the pier is the obvious star, but there's lots more to fill a day. Sea Life Adventure on the Eastern Esplanade is a good indoor option for families when the weather turns, and the Pier Museum tells the long story of the pier, its trains and its many ups and downs over the years.

West of the pier, Cliff Gardens climb the slopes above the seafront, with winding paths and lovely estuary views. The Southend Cliff Railway, a little funicular, has carried people up and down the cliff for over a century, though it doesn't run all year, so look before you plan around it. Up on the clifftop, the Cliffs Pavilion hosts shows, comedy and concerts.

Heading east, Thorpe Bay and Shoeburyness have quieter beaches that suit families wanting a bit more space, while Leigh-on-Sea's old fishing town to the west is perfect for a slower wander and seafood by the water.
With the pier, the shops and the seafront all within walking distance, Southend is an easy place to spend a whole day on foot.
